Juniors]]}} {{MedalBronze|[[1996 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|1996 France]]|[[Serbia men's national under-18 basketball team|Under-18 Team]]}} }} '''Igor Rakočević''' ({{lang-sr-cyrl|Игор Ракочевић}}; born 29 March 1978) is a Serbian professional [[basketball]] executive and former player. At a height of 1.94 m (6'4 {{1/2}}") tall,{{cite Sports-Reference |title=Igor Rakočević |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ra/igor-rakocevic-1.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111106001031/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ra/igor-rakocevic-1.html |archive-date=6 November 2011}} he played at both the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions, but he spent the vast majority of his career playing as a shooting guard. During his playing career, Rakočević was a two-time [[All-EuroLeague Team]] member, and a three-time [[Alphonso Ford EuroLeague Top Scorer Trophy]] winner. He was also a member of the senior [[FR Yugoslavian national basketball team|FR Yugoslavian national team]], which was eventually renamed the Serbian and Montenegrin national team. With FR Yugoslavia, he won gold medals at both the [[2001 FIBA EuroBasket]] and the [[2002 FIBA World Championship]]. ==Professional career== ===Early years=== Rakočević played with [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] and [[KK Budućnost Podgorica|Budućnost]] before going to the [[NBA]]. With Crvena zvezda, he won the [[YUBA League]] championship in the 1997–98 season, and finished second in the [[FIBA Korać Cup]] in the [[1997–98 FIBA Korać Cup|same season]]. In 2000, after getting drafted in the NBA, he signed a three-year contract with KK Budućnost, with an NBA exit clause along with a set transfer fee should he decide to exercise the clause. ===Minnesota Timberwolves=== Rakočević was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], in the 2nd round (51st overall) of the [[2000 NBA draft]].[http://www.nba.com/history/draft/2000-draft/ NBA Draft history: 2000 Draft] He did not play in the [[NBA]], until the [[2002–03 NBA season]], in which he totaled 244 minutes of playing time, in 42 games played, and averaged 1.9 points, 0.8 assists, and 0.4 rebounds per game. He was released after the season, and signed by the [[San Antonio Spurs]], who also released him shortly after. The 2002 - 2003 season ended up being his only season in the NBA, with his final game being a 97–78 win over the Portland Trail Blazers on April 6, 2003. In his final game, Rakočević played for 1 minute and recorded 1 assist and no other stats. ===Back to Europe=== In October 2003, Rakočević returned to Europe, and signed with Crvena zvezda,[http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2003&mm=10&dd=07&nav_id=121298 Rakočević potpisao ugovor sa Crvenom zvezdom] (Serbian) where he was [[Adriatic League Top Scorer|the top scorer of the Adriatic League]]. He was the [[Captain (sports)|captain]] and best player of Crvena zvezda in that 2003–04 season. He continued his career in Spain, where he played with [[Pamesa Valencia]], [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] and [[Saski Baskonia|Tau Cerámica]]. In the [[Euroleague 2006–07|EuroLeague 2006–07]] season, he won the [[Alphonso Ford EuroLeague Top Scorer Trophy]].[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/11387/tau-s-rakocevic-wins-race-for-alphonso-ford-trophy Tau's Rakocevic wins race for Alphonso Ford Trophy] He was also selected to the [[All-EuroLeague]] Second Team of that year's competition.[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/12172/all-euroleague-team-mvp-announced All-Euroleague team, MVP announced] With TAU Cerámica, Rakočević won the [[Spanish Basketball Supercup|Spanish Supercup]] title in 2006, 2007, and 2008, the [[Spanish Basketball King's Cup|Spanish King's Cup]] title in [[Copa del Rey de Baloncesto 2008-09|2009]], and the [[Spanish ACB League]] championship in 2008. He also won another Alphonso Ford Top Scorer Trophy with TAU, in 2009. In June 2009, he signed a three-year contract with the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]] club [[Efes Pilsen SK|Efes Pilsen]].[http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2009&mm=06&dd=19&nav_id=367016 B92.net Rakočević u Efesu!] Rakočević made his debut with the senior [[FR Yugoslavia national basketball team|FR Yugoslavian national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2000 Summer Olympic Games]]. After that, he played at the [[2001 EuroBasket]], in Turkey (where he won a gold medal), and at the [[2005 EuroBasket]], in [[Serbia and Montenegro]]. He was a member of the FR Yugoslavia team that became the [[FIBA World Championship|FIBA World Champions]] in [[Indianapolis]], at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship]], and he was the [[Captain (sports)|captain]] of the [[Serbia and Montenegro national basketball team|Serbia and Montenegro national team]] in Japan, at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]. He also played at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Athens Summer Olympic Games]]. == Post-playing career == In February 2015, Rakočević was elected as the vice-president of the [[Basketball Federation of Serbia]], and put in charge of men's basketball.{{cite web |title=Igor Rakočević novi potpredsednik KSS-a: Velika čast i odgovornost |url=https://sport.blic.rs/kosarka/domaca-kosarka-i-aba/igor-rakocevic-novi-potpredsednik-kss-a-velika-cast-i-odgovornost/s5msd3n |website=sport.blic.rs |access-date=12 August 2018}} In December 2020, he was not sought for re-election.{{cite web |title="POSAO SAM RADIO POŠTENO, SAVESNO I POSVEĆENO" Igor Rakočević napustio KSS, a evo KO DOLAZI na njegovo mesto |url=https://sport.blic.rs/kosarka/domaca-kosarka-i-aba/igor-rakocevic-vise-nije-potpredsednik-kss-na-njegovo-mesto-dolazi-krstic/7qd3een |website=sport.blic.rs |access-date=14 December 2020}} Rakočević was elected on 5-year [[Term of office|term]] as a member of the Assembly of the [[KK Crvena zvezda]] on 27 December 2021.{{cite web |title=Čović još pet godina na čelu Zvezde, najveći saziv guard]] position with [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]].[http://www.euroleague.net/features/blog/2009-2010/vladimir-stankovic/i/66177/4128/the-excitement-starts-here Euroleague - Vladimir Stanković:
